Mapping Between Period Labels

Source: R/period_mapping.R
period_mapping.Rd

Create a mapping depicting the relationship between labels_x and labels_y. The types of relationship that can be mapped are:

  • "labels_x equals labels_y"

  • "labels_x contains labels_y"

  • "labels_x is contained in labels_y"

  • "labels_x overlaps with labels_y".

Usage

period_mapping(
  labels_x,
  labels_y = NULL,
  relation = c("equals", "contains", "is_contained_in", "overlaps_with"),
  format = c("tibble", "matrix"),
  name_x = "x",
  name_y = "y",
  interpret_single = c("lower", "upper"),
  interpret_multi = NULL,
  interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent")
)

Arguments

labels_x

Vector of period labels.

labels_y

Vector of period labels or NULL.

relation

Relationship between labels. Choices are "equals" (the default), "contains", "is_contained_in", and "overlaps_with". See below for details and examples.

format

Format of return value. Choices are "tibble" (the default) or "matrix".

name_x, name_y

Names for the two sides of the mapping in the return value. Defaults are "x" and "y". Applied to tibble columns and to matrix dimnames.

interpret_single

How to interpret a label for a single year, such as "2020". Choices are "lower" (the default) and "upper". See below for details.

interpret_multi

How to interpret a label that refers to multiple years, such as "2020-2025". Choices are NULL (the default), "at_upper", and "below_upper". See below for details.

interpret_fail

Action if element of labels cannot be interpreted. Choices are "error" (the default), "warn", and "silent".

Value

Tibble or matrix, depending on the value of format.

Details

If no value for labels_y is supplied, labels_x is mapped onto itself.

Tibbles produced by period_mapping() are sparse in that they only include matches. Matrices produced by period_mapping() are dense in that they include matches and non-matches. See the example below.

The relation argument

relationEndpoints of labels_x and labels_y
"equals"Endpoints equal
"contains"Endpoints of labels_y inside endpoints of labels_x
"is_contained_in"Endpoints of labels_x inside endpoints of labels_y
"overlaps_with"Endpoint of labels_x in labels_y, or reverse

Rules for interpreting inputs

Single-year

Labels for single-year periods sometimes refer to the lower limits of periods, and sometimes refer to upper limits. For instance, the label "2020" is sometimes used to refer to the period that starts at midnight on 1 January 2020 and ends at midnight on 1 January 2021, and is sometimes used to refer to the period that starts at midnight on 1 July 2019 and ends at midnight on 1 July 2020.

The interpret_single argument can be used to distinguish between the two conventions:

interpret_singleRuleExample
"lower""a" -> [a,a+1)"2020" -> [2020,2021)
"upper""a" -> [a-1,a)"2020" -> [2019,2020)

Multi-year

In labels for multi-year periods, the second number is sometimes the upper limit of the period, and sometimes the upper limit minus 1. For instance, the period that starts at midnight on 1 January 2020 and ends at midnight on 1 January 2025 is sometimes labelled "2020-2025" and is sometimes labelled "2020-2024".

The interpret_multi argument can be used to distinguish between the two conventions:

interpret_multiRuleExample
"at_upper""a-b" -> [a,b)"2020-2025" -> [2020,2025)
"below_upper""a-b" -> [a,b+1)"2020-2024" -> [2020,2025)

If interpret_multi is NULL (the default), then multi-year labels are interpreted using the "at_upper" convention. If, however, the "at_upper" convention leads to intervals with widths 4, 9, 14, ..., then agetime emits a message. Supplying an explicit value for interpret_multi silences this message.

Open

A period that is open on the left has no lower limit, and a period that is open on the right has no upper limit. Labels for open periods are not affected by interpret_single or interpret_multi.

Some examples of open periods:

LabelInterval
"<2000", "before 2000", "under 2000"(-Inf,2000)
"2000 or earlier", "up to 2000"(-Inf,2001)
"2000+", "2000 or more", "2000 or later"[2000,Inf)

Labels starting with "-", such as "-2000", are not accepted.

See also

  • period_coarsen_to() Recode labels into another classification

  • age_mapping() Age equivalent of period_mapping()

  • cohort_mapping() Cohort equivalent of period_mapping()

Examples

x <- c("2020-2025", "2030", "2025-2027")
y <- c("2025-2030", "2020-2025", "2026-2034")
period_mapping(labels_x = x, labels_y = y)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   x         y        
#>   <chr>     <chr>    
#> 1 2020-2025 2020-2025
period_mapping(labels_x = x, labels_y = y, format = "matrix")
#>            y
#> x           2025-2030 2020-2025 2026-2034
#>   2020-2025         0         1         0
#>   2030              0         0         0
#>   2025-2027         0         0         0
period_mapping(labels_x = x, labels_y = y, relation = "contains")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   x         y        
#>   <chr>     <chr>    
#> 1 2020-2025 2020-2025
period_mapping(labels_x = x, labels_y = y, relation = "is_contained_in")
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>   x         y        
#>   <chr>     <chr>    
#> 1 2025-2027 2025-2030
#> 2 2020-2025 2020-2025
#> 3 2030      2026-2034
period_mapping(labels_x = x, labels_y = y, relation = "overlaps_with")
#> # A tibble: 4 × 2
#>   x         y        
#>   <chr>     <chr>    
#> 1 2025-2027 2025-2030
#> 2 2020-2025 2020-2025
#> 3 2030      2026-2034
#> 4 2025-2027 2026-2034

# sparse tibble vs dense matrix
x <- c("2020-2025", "2030-2035")
y <- c("2020-2025", "2025-2030")
period_mapping(labels_x = x, labels_y = y) # one match
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   x         y        
#>   <chr>     <chr>    
#> 1 2020-2025 2020-2025
period_mapping(labels_x = x, labels_y = y, format = "matrix")
#>            y
#> x           2020-2025 2025-2030
#>   2020-2025         1         0
#>   2030-2035         0         0

# map labels_x onto itself
x <- c("2020--2025", "2020-2025", "2030")
period_mapping(x)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 2
#>   x          y         
#>   <chr>      <chr>     
#> 1 2020--2025 2020--2025
#> 2 2020-2025  2020--2025
#> 3 2020--2025 2020-2025 
#> 4 2020-2025  2020-2025 
#> 5 2030       2030
